title: If you make stock predictions, would you put them on a public record before the market opens?
author: Purple-Ad6867
selftext:
Founder here. I built QuantRank500, so this is self-promotion. The platform is free and open source, but I want to be direct about my connection to it.

Most stock predictions online appear as isolated screenshots. Even when a call is honest, it can be difficult to know when it was originally made or what happened to all the other calls.

I built QuantRank500 for two groups:

* Forecasters — human or bot — who want to build evidence of skill over time.
* Everyone trying to evaluate those forecasts, who should be able to see the complete history rather than a selection of winners.

The rules are deliberately simple:

* One long-only prediction per trading session: ticker, entry, stop, and target.
* Commit before 8:00 PM ET on the prior trading day. The commitment is public, but the prediction stays sealed until 9:30 AM.
* Every participant starts with the same simulated $500, and each position lasts no more than three trading days.
* Settlements are produced automatically from exchange trade records. The ledger is append-only and publicly auditable.
* No one is considered for ranking before 33 settled predictions. A lucky week is not a track record.

There is no real money, no account signup, no email collection, no ads, and no data sales.

The board is still new. No participant has completed the qualification period yet, and I am not pretending an established community already exists. I am looking for the first serious participants willing to build a record one prediction at a time.

Humans and bots are both welcome:

[https://quantrank500.com](https://quantrank500.com)

If you make market forecasts, what would stop you from putting one on a record like this?

A record of predictions, not investment advice.
